Sandbox_Trains.TopSpeed_tooltip: The fastest any train goes, in tiles a second, at the middle of a run between two stops. Every train leaves and arrives at the same moment, so the longest run on the map at this speed decides how long every run takes. Past about 11, somebody running forward along a roof moves faster than the 20 a multiplayer server allows: leave Speed anti-cheat at Relax for the trains.
Sandbox_Trains.Dwell_tooltip: How long every train waits at a stop, in seconds of play. Getting on and off is only possible while it waits.
Sandbox_Trains.SpeedCheck_tooltip: Multiplayer only. The inside of a train car is a long way from the train, and going through a car's door moves a player further in one step than a server whose AntiCheatSpeed kicks or bans will allow. Relax for the trains sets AntiCheatSpeed to log while the server runs (the .ini is not changed). Leave it as set keeps the server's setting, and a player walking a train through its cars may then be kicked.
Sandbox_Trains.Circle_tooltip: The line round the whole map on the game's own track: Ekron, Irvington, March Ridge, Muldraugh, the junction by West Point, Fallas Lake, Riverside, Brandenburg. Does not run: no train of it exists. Takes effect at once.
Sandbox_Trains.Louisville_tooltip: The line from the junction by West Point through West Point and Valley Station into Louisville, run out and back. Does not run: no train of it exists. Takes effect at once.
Sandbox_Trains.Halts_tooltip: The halts between towns keep every run about the same length, so no train has to hurry. Towns only: trains call at the towns and nowhere else, the runs are longer, and every run takes as long as the longest of them.
Sandbox_Trains.Fleet_tooltip: On a loop: a train to every stop, so one is at every stop every time the trains stand; or to every second, third or fourth stop; or one train on each line and no more. A line run out and back has two trains, or one. Fewer trains is some of them missing: the rest keep their names, their cars and what is in them.
Sandbox_Trains.Length_tooltip: Every train has a locomotive at each end, a galley, a hospital car and a private car. Long adds 8 to 18 more cars, Medium 3 to 7, Short 2 or 3. Changing this changes which car is which in every train: every car's room is emptied and furnished afresh. Set it before anybody moves in.
Sandbox_Trains.Empties_tooltip: How many empty boxcars every train has to build in, as well as its other cars. They are coupled on behind the rest, before the rear locomotive. Not used where every train is exactly the cars you wrote. More or fewer moves nothing: every other car keeps its room and what is in it, and an empty that is taken away comes back as it was left.
Sandbox_Trains.Consist: Every train is exactly these cars
Sandbox_Trains.Consist_tooltip: Leave empty for trains made up by the world's own dice. Or write the cars of every train, front first, with commas between: loco, coach, galley, loco. One word is a train of one car. The kinds: loco, coach, commuter, parlor, sleeper, dorm, private, galley, dining, lounge, hospital, survivor, warehouse, baggage, mail, reefer, greenhouse, livestock, workshop, generator, armory, library, chapel, observation, caboose, box, tank, flat, gondola. Thirty cars at most. Changing this empties every car's room.
Sandbox_Trains.Names_tooltip: Leave empty for the mod's own names. Or write names with commas between, in the order the trains are numbered: the circle's first, then the Louisville line's two, then your own lines' in the order they were laid. A train you give no name keeps the mod's.
Sandbox_Trains.Cord_tooltip: Yes: anybody aboard can stop their train between stations; it stands 45 seconds and makes the time up. No: trains stop at stops and nowhere else for anybody aboard.
Sandbox_Trains.Flag_tooltip: Yes: somebody beside the track can ask the next train to stop for them there, and a train somebody is waiting for by name stops for them. No: trains are boarded at stops only.
Sandbox_Trains.PlowPlayers_tooltip: Yes: a player in the way of a moving train is thrown clear and hurt. No: a train passes through a player as if they were not there. The dead are killed and thrown either way.
Sandbox_Trains.Claims_tooltip: How many trains one player may claim as their own, from aboard. A train's owner can lock any of its cars, or all of them, so that nobody else goes in; and can close the whole train, so that nobody else boards it at all, not even to ride its roofs. 0: nobody can own a train, and every lock and closed train is set aside for as long as this is 0. An admin goes anywhere, and can end anybody's claim from the admin's menu. Somebody who already owns more than this keeps them.
Sandbox_Trains.OnMap_tooltip: Yes: every train is marked on every player's map where it is now. No: a train is found by going to its track, or from the menu of a train a player has made theirs.
Sandbox_Trains.Plates_tooltip: Yes: every car with a room inside says what it is on a plate on each side: GALLEY, MEDICAL, SLEEPER. No: a car is known by going into it.
Sandbox_Trains.Sidings_tooltip: The trains go round the cars the map has parked on its own track, at Ekron, Muldraugh and Louisville. Yes: the server lays track there for them to go round on, and takes down the lengths of fence in the way, when a player first comes near. No: nothing in the world is changed, and the trains go round over bare ground. Track already laid stays.
Sandbox_Trains.Water_tooltip: Yes: every sink, bath, shower, rain barrel and water trough in a car is kept full while somebody is in the car, whoever put it there. No: what is in them is all there is.
Sandbox_Trains.Power_tooltip: Yes: every car has power while somebody is in it, for whatever stands in it. No: no car has power of its own. Mind that a generator run inside a car fills the car with its fumes.
Sandbox_Trains.Garden_tooltip: What the beds of a greenhouse car hold when somebody first goes into it. Sown and looked after: the game's own crops, most of them ripe, and they are watered, cured and kept from going over for as long as this is set. Sown: the same crops, and looking after them is the players' work. Bare soil: beds to dig and sow. Whichever it is, a crop in any car grows as in a greenhouse, and is picked, dug up and sown again like any other.
Sandbox_Trains.Animals_tooltip: What a livestock car holds when somebody first goes into it. Animals, fed: three hens and a cockerel, a ewe and a ram, and their feed trough is filled whenever it is empty and somebody is in the car. Animals: the same animals, and feeding them is the players' work. No animals: the stable and its troughs, empty.
Sandbox_Trains.Lead_tooltip: Yes: animals on a rope go into a car with whoever leads them, from a platform while the train stands, and come out with them by the side door at a stop. No: an animal goes aboard only in somebody's arms.
Sandbox_Trains.RoomsX: The cars' insides: map cell, east
Sandbox_Trains.RoomsX_tooltip: Leave this and the next setting alone unless a world will not load with this mod and another mod that has a map of its own. The inside of every car is a room far off the edge of the map: in the map cell this many east and (the next setting) south, and one cell to each train going east from it, forty in all. The mod's own empty map is under cells 96 to 137 east, 19 to 21 south. Anywhere else the server clears the ground round each room as somebody first goes in. Changing either empties every car's room.
Sandbox_Trains.RoomsY: The cars' insides: map cell, south
Sandbox_Trains.RoomsY_tooltip: See the setting before this one. Keep the rooms two cells or more from any other mod's map.
